accessible_name: Definition 9: Derivation
listen_text: Definition 9: Derivation A derivation of a sentence formula A from assumptions Gamma is a finite tree of sentences satisfying the following conditions: Item 1. The topmost sentences of the tree are either in Gamma or are discharged by an inference in the tree. Item 2. The bottommost sentence of the tree is formula A. Item 3. Every sentence in the tree except the sentence formula A at the bottom is a premise of a correct application of an inference rule whose conclusion stands directly below that sentence in the tree. We then say that formula A is the conclusion of the derivation and Gamma its undischarged assumptions. If a derivation of formula A from Gamma exists, we say that formula A is derivable from Gamma, or in symbols: Gamma syntactically derives A. If there is a derivation of formula A in which every assumption is discharged, we write A is derivable without undischarged assumptions.

ordered_steps: Definition 9: Derivation
A derivation of a sentence formula A from assumptions Gamma is a finite tree of sentences satisfying the following conditions:
Item 1.
The topmost sentences of the tree are either in Gamma or are discharged by an inference in the tree.
Item 2.
The bottommost sentence of the tree is formula A.
Item 3.
Every sentence in the tree except the sentence formula A at the bottom is a premise of a correct application of an inference rule whose conclusion stands directly below that sentence in the tree.
We then say that formula A is the conclusion of the derivation and Gamma its undischarged assumptions.

If a derivation of formula A from Gamma exists, we say that formula A is derivable from Gamma, or in symbols: Gamma syntactically derives A. If there is a derivation of formula A in which every assumption is discharged, we write A is derivable without undischarged assumptions.

It is best to write down the assumptions involved and label the inference rules as you progress, so it is easy to see whether all assumptions have been discharged at the end of the proof. Step 2 applies the conjunction elimination rule to 1 and concludes formula A. Step 3 applies the conditional introduction rule to 2 and concludes if A and B, then A. The final conclusion is if A and B, then A. We now have a correct derivation of if A and B, then A.
